newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador hopes for IMF stand-by deal in October.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador hopes for IMF stand-by deal in October.

text.p: Ecuador hopes to reach a deal on a stand-by agreement with the International Monetary Fund in October, a government official said Monday.
"Our ambition is that the deal will be ready in October," the official at the Finance Ministry, who requested anonymity, told Reuters.
The deal is likely to help Ecuador to renegotiate its Paris Club debt, he said.
During a visit to the country by IMF officials recently, government sources said Ecuador hoped to reach a stand-by agreement with the IMF, but without any disbursements.
Separately, Ecuador's 1997 budget deficit could come in at two percent of gross domestic product, lower than the government's forecast, the source added.
"We are expecting a deficit of two percent of GDP," he said.
President Fabian Alarcon forecast earlier in the year a 1997 budget deficit of 2.5 to 2.7 percent of GDP.

The official said it was possible to reach a deficit of 2.0 percent of GDP, even when counting a special contingency fund to deal with the affects of "El Nino" -- the periodic climatic phenomenon that warms the waters of the eastern Pacific Ocean.
Meteorologists have identified the build-up of a strong Nino this year. The warmer weather has already led to heavy rains and landslides, damaging agricultural crops.
The official said the government is working on creating the conditions for any new debt issues in the domestic market to have maturities of more than five years.
